text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Before your first visit, review the client file with your team leader and confirm the household has agreed to receive you. Each volunteer in the Kisaro Hope Circle programme is assigned no more than six households, and visits should take place at least twice a month. During a visit, check that the client has enough medication for the next 14 days and ask gently about missed doses. Do not ask questions about how the client became infected, and never discuss their status with neighbours or relatives who have not been told. In 2023, volunteers who followed this checklist recorded 92% adherence among their clients. If a client reports fever, weight loss or a new cough, refer them to the Mbuyu clinic within 48 hours.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the 140 community health workers deployed across Ndaraweti District completed 18,450 household visits, slightly above the target of 18,000. Coverage was strongest in the lowland wards, where each worker reached an average of 31 households per month. In the three highland wards, however, visits fell to 19 households per worker because heavy rains washed out two footbridges in April. Referral slips were returned for 64% of children referred with danger signs, up from 51% in the previous period. Stock-outs remain a concern: 22 workers reported no zinc tablets for more than three weeks, and the district store did not resupply them until late May. Supervisors have not yet completed the planned refresher training on newborn care.

passages.source_passage: The board will be pleased to hear that the Tumaini Savings Circles programme now supports 212 groups in Lubero and Kasiva counties, up from 168 at our last meeting in March. Members have saved a combined 4.3 million shillings this cycle, and loan repayment stands at 96 percent. Women make up roughly four in five members. Not every group has performed well: nine groups in Kasiva did not complete their share-out in September after a dispute over record keeping, and two treasurers have since resigned. Field officers are retraining these groups on the passbook system. We do not recommend opening new groups in Kasiva until the remaining disputes are resolved, and management asks the board to approve a three-month pause there.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023 programme year, the Lamplight Evening Classes network ran 37 classes in church halls, schools and one converted bus depot across the Oruma valley. Enrolment reached 864 adults, of whom 71% were women over the age of thirty. By the final assessment, 512 learners could read a short notice and write their own name and village, compared with fewer than a hundred at intake. Attendance dipped during the harvest months, and we did not meet our target of keeping every class open through October. Four classes closed early because facilitators could not travel after dark once the road lighting failed. Learners told us that being able to read a clinic card was the change that mattered most, not the certificate.

passages.source_passage: During the 2024 long rains, the Green Furrow project distributed drought-tolerant sorghum and cowpea seed to 1,250 farming households in Merekani and Sololo sub-counties. Field monitors visited a sample of 300 plots in July. Average sorghum yields on project plots were 1.4 tonnes per hectare, against 0.9 tonnes on neighbouring plots planted with local maize. Rainfall was about 40 percent below the ten-year average, so the comparison is encouraging. However, uptake of water-harvesting pits was lower than planned: only 85 households dug pits, and many said they did not have the labour to do so. Monitors found no evidence that seed had been resold, though some families shared seed with relatives who were not enrolled.

passages.source_passage: Over the past year, the Little Steps playgroup network grew from 18 to 26 sites in the hill settlements around Vashti Lake. Each playgroup meets three mornings a week and is led by two trained caregivers, most of them mothers from the same village. In total, 640 children aged three to five attended at least once, and roughly two-thirds attended regularly. Developmental screening in November showed that 58% of regular attenders met age-appropriate language milestones, compared with 41% at baseline in 2022. We were not able to open the planned site at Koru Ridge because no suitable building was available. Caregivers also told us that fathers rarely came to parent sessions, and we have not yet found a format that suits their working hours.

passages.source_passage: The Sabaki Coast bed net campaign distributed 48,600 long-lasting insecticidal nets between 3 and 21 March 2024, reaching 97% of registered households in the target wards. Distribution teams used household registers compiled in January, allocating one net for every two people. Post-distribution checks in a sample of 450 homes found that 81% of nets were hanging over a sleeping space. In the fishing villages of Mtongwe, however, several families were using nets to dry fish or fence vegetable plots, and teams did not have enough replacement nets to correct this. Households headed by older people were less likely to have hung their nets, often because they had no one to help fix the hooks. No serious adverse reactions to the insecticide were reported.

passages.source_passage: Since 2019, the Haki Njema Paralegal Service has trained 64 community paralegals across the four rural districts of Ulanga Province. Most residents live more than 50 kilometres from the nearest magistrate's court, and the province has only seven practising advocates, none of whom are based outside the provincial capital. Land disputes and inheritance claims by widows account for around 60% of the cases our paralegals receive. In our 2023 caseload review, nearly half of the women who approached us did not know they had any legal right to their late husband's land. Paralegals do not represent clients in court; instead, they mediate, draft letters and accompany clients to land boards. This proposal seeks support to extend the service to two districts that currently have no paralegal coverage at all.

passages.source_passage: The 14 villages of Bweyale ward, home to roughly 9,800 people, rely on two functioning boreholes and a seasonal stream for drinking water. A third borehole drilled in 2016 has not worked since its hand pump failed in 2021, and no spare parts are stocked locally. Women and girls walk an average of 3.5 kilometres for each collection trip during the dry season. A household survey conducted by Clearwell Rural Trust in February found that only 23% of households had a latrine with a slab, and open defecation was reported in every village. Diarrhoea was the leading reason for child clinic visits last year. Earlier hygiene campaigns were not followed by investment in facilities, and residents told us they did not see lasting change.

passages.source_passage: At the mid-term point in June 2024, the Safe Hearth foster care and family tracing service had placed 118 separated children with approved foster families across Nyaweru and Tolo districts. Tracing officers reunited 47 children with parents or close relatives, and follow-up visits found that 42 of these placements were stable after six months. The evaluation team found that caseworkers were carrying an average of 35 cases each, well above the agreed ceiling of 20. As a result, not all foster homes received the monthly visit required by the protocol. No child in the sample reported physical abuse in foster care, though several older children said they had not been asked for their views before being placed. The team recommends recruiting four additional caseworkers before the end of the year.
